labels.notes: Read off the elaborated type (Expr.and? split, then getAppFn of each conjunct, and getUsedConstants). halfLightLine_dual_separates_causallyOpenFuture has the 11 positive conjuncts Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal (applied to halfLightLine.dual.toPrecausality, the ladder's lean for absolutely_minimal with lean_form's subject C.toPrecausality; no Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal exists to shadow it), Causality.CausallyArcConnected, PushUp, LocallyPushUp, IsCausal, GloballyHyperbolic, CausallyCompact, StronglyCausalOpen, StronglyCausal, HasTimeFunction and CurvesExtend. Each is applied to Causal.Causality.dual Causal.halfLightLine. #print of every definition agrees with the ladder's `what`. halfLightLine_dual_absolutelyMinimalOn (W : Opens R) states Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimalOn halfLightLine.dual.toPrecausality W. #print gives: for every S covering W and every open V <= W, le_V (resp. lt_V) is a TransGen of le (resp. lt) on V inf O, O in S. Universally closed in W, this is 'absolutely minimal on every open set for every cover of it'. It has the same form as halfLightLine_absolutelyMinimalOn (Causal/Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:165), which kb/0074 and OQ-69 (registers/DECISIONS.md:225) call the gluing reading of defi:causalite 'as OQ-18 describes it'. It was proved for the dual itself (dual_causallyArcConnectedOn on W, then CausallyArcConnectedOn.absolutelyMinimalOn) and is not inferred. Closed statements, no hypothesis. Every evidence citation the REPORT checks resolves at the stated line (ArcConnected.lean:182, Minimal.lean:61, Properties.lean:198 and :210, PushUp.lean:96, LadderLocal.lean:264 and :447, Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:165, :219, :232, :369 and :432). The mark is a target sub-label in the convention of Causal.Dec8MinimalWitness and Causal.RationalLineExtras. No ETT label is marked, as the dispatch requires.

labels.label: T-abs-halflit-dual-separates/2-time-function
labels.notes: Causal.Causality.dual_hasTimeFunction : forall {M} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M}, C.dual.HasTimeFunction <-> C.HasTimeFunction. #print HasTimeFunction gives: exists T, Continuous T and (forall x y, C.le top x y -> x != y -> T x < T y). The statement is true. C.dual.le top x y is C.le top y x, so T works for C exactly when -T works for C.dual, and the proof's `key` maps T to fun x => -T x in both directions. halfLightLine_dual_hasTimeFunction is dual_hasTimeFunction.2 halfLightLine_hasTimeFunction. The latter's witness is id (Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:332), so the dual's witness is -id, as the title asks. The statement is existential; -id is the proof term's witness. No duplicate exists. Under `import Causal` (all 248 root imports), no constant other than the new ones has a type mentioning both HasTimeFunction and Causality.dual or Precausality.dual, and env.contains is false for all six new full names. The nearest lemma is Causal.Causality.dual_isTimeFunction (Causal/Morphism.lean:907), about IsTimeFunction, ETT's defi:fonction_temps: a strong morphism to timelikeLine. That is a different notion (Causal/CurvesExtend.lean:510-515 says HasTimeFunction 'must not be read as' it), and its full name differs. The new lemma is general and model-free. The closer's suggestion to hoist it next to HasTimeFunction in Causal.CurvesExtend under the same full name is sound.

labels.label: T-abs-halflit-dual-separates/3-not-causally-open-future
labels.notes: halfLightLine_dual_not_locallyCausallyOpenFuture : not halfLightLine.dual.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture. #print gives: forall x, exists W, x in W and CausallyOpenFutureOn W, i.e. J+_U(V) is open for all opens V <= U <= W. It is proved by causal_ladder, with the dual's absolute minimality as a `have`. The rule used is AbsolutelyMinimal.causallyOpenFuture_of_locallyCausallyOpenFuture (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:264, attribute at Causal/Ladder/Rules.lean:54). The contradiction is halfLightLine_not_causallyOpenPast (Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:219), which is literally not halfLightLine.dual.CausallyOpenFuture, the ladder's causally_open_future of the dual. The direct form at 0 is halfLightLine_not_causallyOpenPastOn_of_zero_mem (:232): not halfLightLine.dual.CausallyOpenFutureOn W for every W containing 0. It is cited, not restated, as disclosed. The two-sided negations (not CausallyOpen, not LocallyCausallyOpen) follow by causal_ladder through causally_open => causally_open_future and locally_causally_open => locally_causally_open_future. Both are ladder edges. Mathematics: the dual's J+_M((1,2)) is the half-lit line's J-_M((1,2)) = [0,2), which is not open.

labels.label: T-abs-halflit-dual-separates/4-separation
labels.notes: The elaborated statement has 18 conjuncts. 11 are positive (above). 7 are negated: CausallyOpenFuture, LocallyCausallyOpenFuture, CausallyOpen, LocallyCausallyOpen, Tarentin, ChronalNeighbours and CausallyPlain, each Causal.Causality.<X> halfLightLine.dual, and each the `lean` field of its [[property]] in programme/ladder.toml. This is halfLightLine_separates_causallyOpen's list (Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:369) with CausallyOpenFuture and LocallyCausallyOpenFuture moved to the negative side, as the REPORT says. Every for_keeper `from` id (the 11 positives) is a conjunct, and so is every `to` (2 proposed, 5 optional). not_locallyCausallyOpenFuture_of_causallyArcConnected_bare : not (forall C : Causality R, C.CausallyArcConnected -> C.GloballyHyperbolic -> C.PushUp -> C.LocallyCausallyOpenFuture). This is the library's `_bare` form: a refuted universal implication over Causality R, with the model unnamed. Its name follows not_<conclusion>_of_<main hypothesis>_bare, with the extra hypotheses left out of the name, exactly as not_causallyOpen_of_causallyArcConnected_bare (Dec8MinimalWitness.lean:415) and not_causallyOpenFuture_of_pushUp_of_locallyCausallyOpen_bare (PushUpNotOpen.lean:346) do. The docstring's 'hence -> causally_open_future' is a correct contrapositive through causally_open_future => locally_causally_open_future. No metric notion appears in any statement. The constants are R, Opens R, the ladder predicates and Causality.dual; Real.pseudoMetricSpace appears only as the instance path of R's topology.
